svg.title: GALTON: how a diffusion model turns static into a picture
svg.desc: Three steps. One: a photo plus many small random kicks per pixel becomes static; the kicks pile into a bell curve, like balls through a Galton board. Two: the model is trained to guess the kicks that were added, and is scored against the kicks really added. Three: start from fresh static, subtract the model's guess a little at a time, and repeat until a new picture appears. Illustration: the pixel grids stand in for Stable Diffusion v1, which adds its noise to a 64 by 64 by 4 latent, not to the pixels.
svg.text: ILLUSTRATION · PIXEL GRIDS STAND IN FOR STABLE DIFFUSION V1'S 64×64×4 LATENT
1 Photo + many small random kicks = static
2 The model learns to guess the kicks
SCORED AGAINST THE KICKS REALLY ADDED. THAT IS THE WHOLE TRAINING JOB.
FRESH STATIC IS DRAWN FROM THE SAME BELL, SO NO PHOTO IS NEEDED TO START.
SOURCES: HO, JAIN, ABBEEL 2020 (DDPM) · COMPVIS STABLE-DIFFUSION V1 CODE. ORIGINAL HUBERT DIAGRAM.
